body: If `some_func` raises an exception, the second `print` will never be executed because the exception will be re-raised at the end of the `finally` block. So I think that means no error should be generated for the final line of the code sample.

Yep, good find! This only occurs with nested statements because we have to do a ~hack~ clever trick with [disable_branch_skip](https://github.com/python/mypy/blob/d391f108c195533a5800afe73f5b3257babc83a3/mypy/partially_defined.py#L497). 

We can probably do something smarter here and only report errors in `finally` blocks when we're in `disable_branch_skip` mode.

I don't really have time to work on this right now, so happy for someone else to pick it up. Otherwise, I could probably start in February.

Not entirely sure if this is the same issue or a separate issue, but we are also seeing this where an `except` then `break`s from a loop:
https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/blob/63f83a0f916ee5030ee0f2dad3ba999b325c167c/aiohttp/web_protocol.py#L540-L549
Is there still an issue here? If so, could someone provide a self-contained minimal code sample?

The original example still reproduces (again, remember to enable the error code). It currently produces possibly-undefined on line 7, but not on line 12. As you mentioned above, there should be no errors, as the exception is reraised.

In the linked example from aiohttp, we do a `break` in the exception handler, so also should not get any errors. However, a minimal example with break doesn't produce an error, so not sure why it behaves differently on our code base.

Here’s the example as a playground link (using [inline configuration](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/inline_config.html)):

https://mypy-play.net/?mypy=latest&python=3.11&gist=c74b25457397d60fe5f063151ceb5fee

here's a much simpler example that appears to be an exact duplicate:

```python
def f(x: int) -> None:
    try:
        if x >= 5:
            y = 2
        else:
            raise AssertionError('unreachable')
        print(y)
    finally:
        print('finally!')
```

```console
$ mypy t.py --enable-error-code=possibly-undefined
t.py:7: error: Name "y" may be undefined  [possibly-undefined]
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 1 source file)
```

Another instance from python/typeshed#12151 (when using `--platform win32`):

```python
import sys

try:
    if sys.platform == "win32":
        pip_exe = ""
        reveal_type(pip_exe)  # Revealed type is "builtins.str"
    else:
        pip_exe = ""
    reveal_type(pip_exe)  # Revealed type is "builtins.str"
                          # Name "pip_exe" may be undefined  [possibly-undefined]
finally:
    pass
```
